---
applyTo: "Dockerfile,.dockerignore,.github/workflows/test.yml,.github/workflows/test-docker.yml,.github/workflows/deploy-main.yml"
---

Keep the workspace image based on Ubuntu 26.04 and build it for Linux amd64, the supported Linux architecture of the bundled Lynx runtime. Read Node and Rust versions from `.nvmrc` and `rust-toolchain.toml`, and keep the Corepack version aligned with `.github/actions/pnpm-install/action.yml`.

Share an Ubuntu `base` stage between `builder` and `runtime`. Configure the optional `UBUNTU_MIRROR` argument and install runtime libraries in `base`; install compilers and other build tools only in `builder`. Apply the mirror override to `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources`, preserving suites, components, and the Ubuntu signing keyring. Leave Ubuntu's default sources in place when the argument is unset. Public Volcengine builds have timed out connecting to the default Ubuntu archive and security hosts; use `--build-arg UBUNTU_MIRROR=http://mirrors.volces.com/ubuntu` there. Use `apt-get update --error-on=any` so a failed index download reports the actual network error.

Build npm workspaces through the repository-root Turbo command used by `deploy-main.yml`, excluding both `benchx_cli` and `@lynx-js/benchmark-*`. Keep Wasm packages in this build. Exclude `swc_plugin_reactlynx`, `swc_plugin_reactlynx_compat`, and `web-core` only from the subsequent native Cargo build, and enable `ui_judge/server` to include its optional binary and packaged runtime assets.

Use separate builder and runtime stages. Keep Node, the installed workspace dependency graph, package outputs, and final native deliverables in the runtime image. Preserve `node_modules` from the frozen full install: runtime compilers load workspace packages whose peer links are also development dependencies, so a production-only reinstall removes required links. Accept the larger dependency layer to preserve the original workspace layout and published dependency contracts. Preserve source files exported by workspace packages. Remove Cargo targets, build caches, and generated source maps before copying the workspace into the runtime stage. Copy both Rust executables, the React transform shared library, the generated launcher, the Lynx runtime library, and `lynx_core.js` explicitly. Strip only binaries built here, preserving the downloaded Lynx runtime unchanged. Do not copy native compiler toolchains, the system package manager installation, headers, or download caches into the final image. Use BuildKit cache export `mode=min` so CI builds do not export intermediate builder layers.

Set runtime `LYNX_LIB_PATH` and `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` to the copied assets. The headless runner otherwise retains Cargo-injected paths into the SDK cache removed during cleanup.

Keep JavaScript builds workspace-wide through Turbo. Deployment changes must preserve published packages' dependency declarations and peer compatibility. Do not add hardcoded package lists, global hoisting, tarballs, or installed-manifest patches to Dockerfile. Keep workspace package entry points unchanged.

When validating deployment changes, resolve the compiler from the server package and compile both Web and Native artifacts after a fresh full install, build-artifact cleanup, and relocation, without model credentials or publication.

Export installed `node_modules` directories into a separate tree while preserving their workspace-relative paths and symlinks. Keep downloaded Lynx SDK files separate from Rust outputs. Use independent `COPY --link` layers for Node, installed dependencies, the SDK, workspace files, and compiled Rust deliverables. Remove pnpm installation bookkeeping with variable timestamps and normalize exported timestamps, including symlinks, so unchanged file contents can produce reusable layers across commits. Do not remove source files used by package exports. Dependency splitting must preserve Node resolution through both pnpm links and workspace links. Exclude `.volcengine` from the runtime filesystem.

Do not copy host `node_modules`, Cargo targets, Turbo caches, or local environment files into the Docker build context. Validate the complete Dockerfile in the independent `test-docker.yml` workflow only for pull requests changing `.github/workflows/**`. Start without depending on the Ubuntu build, and keep Docker validation out of `test.yml` and its `done.needs`. Do not add push or merge-group triggers that would run this expensive build unconditionally. Build without pushing images, registry credentials, or `packages: write` permission. Do not build Docker images in `deploy-main.yml`. Pin Docker Actions to verified commit SHAs.
